title: Magnetic and 57Fe Mossbauer Study of the Single Molecule Magnet Behavior of a Dy3Fe7 Coordination Cluster

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, a solution of N-methyldiethanolamine (0.09 g, 0.75 mmol) in 20 mL of MeOH was added dropwise over 20 min to a stirred solution of DyCl3·6H2O (0.07 g, 0.25 mmol), benzoic acid (0.06 g, 0.50 mmol), FeCl3 (0.08 g, 0.50 mmol), and NaN3 (0.034 g, 0.50 mmol) in 20 mL of MeOH. The mixture was heated under reflux for 1 h, cooled to room temperature, and allowed to stand undisturbed in a sealed vial. Orange needles of 1 were obtained after 3 days, collected by filtration, and washed with MeCN.
synthesis.time: 20 min addition; 1 h reflux; 3 days crystallization
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic reflux then standing in a sealed vial
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cooled to room temperature, stood undisturbed in a sealed vial; orange needles collected by filtration and washed with MeCN

properties.summary: Dc and ac susceptibility of 1 show dominant intracluster antiferromagnetic coupling and a ferrimagnetic spin arrangement. Slow magnetization relaxation (SMM behavior) is observed, mainly attributed to Dy(III) anisotropy, with hysteresis below about 1.9–2 K. Powder ac data give Ueff = 30.9 K (τ0 = 1.3×10−7 s); combined single-crystal ac/dc decay data give Ueff = 33.4 K (τ0 = 6.6×10−8 s), reported as the highest barrier then known for a Ln(III)–Fe(III) SMM. Below 0.5 K the hysteresis width becomes temperature-independent (~2 T at 0.035 T/s), indicating a quantum tunneling regime. 57Fe Mössbauer spectra confirm Fe(III) antiferromagnetic coupling and slow relaxation relative to the Larmor time below 35 K.

synthesis.procedure: Orange needles of the methanol solvate 1 were prepared as above. On exposure to air the crystals lose all seven lattice methanol molecules but remain crystalline; the desolvated phase is formulated as the dihydrate from microanalysis. A synchrotron structure of a small air-exposed crystal confirmed that the molecular Dy3Fe7 cluster is essentially unchanged. Crystals remain unchanged in air for at least a year.
synthesis.temperature: air exposure after crystallization of 1; synchrotron data at 150 K
synthesis.time: air exposure; crystals stable for at least one year
synthesis.vessel_or_method: air desolvation of crystals of 1; synchrotron SCD beamline structure of desolvated crystal
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: loss of lattice methanols on exposure to air; remains crystalline as dihydrate

properties.summary: Only crystallographic/microanalytic characterization of the air-desolvated dihydrate is given; magnetic and Mössbauer data are reported for compound 1 without a separate dataset for the desolvated phase.
